chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Asadi al-Barda'i narrated to us. He said: Ruqayya bint Ishaq ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, from her father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:

No servant's feet will move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about four things: about his life and how he spent it, about his youth and how he used it, about his wealth — where he earned it and how he spent it, and about his love for us, the Ahl al-Bayt.

key_terms.أهل البيت: The Ahl al-Bayt, the household of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), a term of central importance in Shia Islam
key_terms.القيامة: The Day of Resurrection, when all humanity will be gathered for judgment
key_terms.حبنا: Our love, i.e., love for the Prophet's family — presented here as a criterion of divine accountability
key_terms.عمره: His lifespan — the totality of time given to a person by God

ai.seo_question: What are the four things a person will be asked about on the Day of Judgment in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) warns that on the Day of Judgment, every person will be held accountable for four things: how they spent their life, how they used their youth, the source and expenditure of their wealth, and their love for the Ahl al-Bayt. This hadith was narrated in a teaching session held in Sha'ban 367 AH, and uniquely adds love for the Prophet's household as a fourth category of accountability, emphasizing its centrality in the Shia tradition.
